result.note: Weekly roundup; tested the end of the exam agitation, the Supreme Court order and the passage of the penalties bill.

questions.prompt: Consider the following statements about the events that ended the exam-reform agitation in July 2026:
items: Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan resigned on 25 July 2026, and the month-long agitation ended hours later.
The Centre's concessions included withdrawing cases against protesters and compensating bereaved families.
The Supreme Court ordered that detained protesters under 18 continue to be held.
questions.ask: How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explain: The third statement is wrong. On 29 July 2026 the Supreme Court ordered under-18s released and police footage preserved. The Centre also conceded exam reform, although the Cockroach Janta Party reported hundreds of fresh arrests and continuing surveillance.
questions.source: Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan resigned on July 25 and the month-long agitation ended hours later, with the Centre conceding exam reform, withdrawn cases, and compensation for bereaved families.

questions.prompt: Consider the following statements about the bill on exam malpractice that Parliament passed in July 2026:
items: The bill, which doubles penalties, was introduced in the Lok Sabha and cleared by both Houses within the same week.
The Rajya Sabha passed the bill before the Lok Sabha did.
questions.ask: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explain: The bill reached the Lok Sabha on Monday 27 July and cleared it on Thursday 30 July. The Rajya Sabha passed it on Friday 31 July, a day after the Lok Sabha, so statement 2 is wrong. The Lok Sabha vote came alongside the first NEET chargesheet.
questions.source: A bill doubling penalties reached the Lok Sabha on Monday, cleared it on Thursday alongside the first NEET chargesheet, and passed the Rajya Sabha on Friday.
